title: The Rookery
summary: The group reaches the Rookery, a crowded crossroads settlement where unusually distinct travelers and locals are everywhere. Eva initially reads the place as proof that the Cadre-like clustering is real.

panelPlan.text: The Rookery is dense, layered and human: boarding rooms, market tables, courtyards and family workshops around several dark fragments some travelers call Sunforge pieces.
Eva clocks Dylan Stator, a masked herbal seller, an immaculate gambler and three other visually memorable people before they cross the first courtyard.
Baird Rook, the local host, greets Jessa by her vehicle and Kael by the name Kael gives him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: There are six of them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Six of what?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You know what.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Interesting people?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Exactly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: That's a pretty broad category.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to the Rookery. Names?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Kael Mack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: Good. Try not to owe anyone by sunset.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: See? Even the welcome is strange.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: You're going to wear me out.

directionInline.text: The Rookery should feel socially dense, not like a parade of themed NPCs. Distinct people have ordinary histories and relationships here.

title: Travelers See Types
summary: Baird dismantles Eva's first pattern by explaining who several 'Cadre' figures actually are: cousins, debtors, seasonal workers and people who have been returning to the Rookery for years.

panelPlan.text: Baird walks Eva and Jessa through the market while doing real social work: settling a tab, checking on a sick vendor and carrying a parcel.
Each visually eccentric person Eva points out turns out to have a mundane reason for being there that locals have known for years.
Dylan Stator appears at a workbench and laughs when Eva asks whether he came because of Kael.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The man with the silver mask.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: Burn scars. My cousin.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The woman with the red birds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: Raises them. Owes me money.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Dylan.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dylan
dialogueInline.text: I can hear you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did you come here because of Kael?

dialogueInline.speaker: Dylan
dialogueInline.text: I came because Baird pays late and feeds well.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: We've been here five minutes and you've already turned his cousin into evidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: I like her.

directionInline.text: Dramatize the breadth/depth principle. The group can notice recurrence while still being wrong about why particular people are present.

title: The Man With Many Names
summary: Dylan has heard the story of 'the man with many names' through ordinary road gossip, but he knows Kael's real name because Tomas at the Last Drop insisted on it.

panelPlan.text: Dylan and Kael work side by side on a simple broken buckle or hand tool, keeping the scene tactile and human rather than technical.
Dylan says the Varnok story has traveled farther than the group realized, accumulating Saye and Merrit in some versions.
Eva is thrilled by the spread until Kael points out that a rumor network can now reproduce the mystery without any new event.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dylan
dialogueInline.text: I heard Varnok was also a general.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: That sounds inconvenient for both men.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dylan
dialogueInline.text: Tomas said your name was Kael.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Tomas is a sensible man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: So the stories are merging.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Stories do that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: But now any town could be expecting him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: So if the next town calls me something else, you won't know whether they heard it on the road.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I hate that. Now we can't tell a new thing from an old story.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I don't think the mystery is doing anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: And that is why Eva keeps talking at you.

directionInline.text: This creates a useful contamination problem: after enough rumor spread, later recognition is not automatically fresh evidence.

title: What Counts as a Sunforge
summary: Veyra tries to classify the dark structures around the Rookery as multiple Sunforge fragments. Baird tells her locals do not consider them the same kind of thing and can trace different pieces to different histories.

panelPlan.text: Veyra compares sketches of three black structures while Baird watches with increasing amusement.
Baird identifies one as an old roof support hauled in by his grandfather, one as a buried object no one has moved, and one as material salvaged from somewhere else entirely.
Eva realizes the traveler's single word may be flattening distinct local categories.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: You have three Sunforge sites inside one settlement.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: No, we don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: I can show you the material resemblance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: You can show me three black things.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Do people here have a common name for them?

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: Yes. Roof. Old black thing. And the bench nobody likes sitting on.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Very rigorous.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: Calling them different things doesn't change what they're made of.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: Maybe not. But knowing what it's made of won't tell you why my grandmother dragged it here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We're seeing the same black material all over the Sunfields.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: And they're seeing the history of the thing in front of them.

directionInline.text: The issue should challenge category confidence without implying locals possess the final truth either.

title: Why Everyone Came
summary: Several unusual travelers independently say they arrived because they heard 'something interesting' was happening in the Rookery. No one can identify a single source, but ordinary rumor is still sufficient to explain the convergence.

panelPlan.text: At supper, Eva asks why people came this week. Answers overlap: a card game, a funeral, cheap rooms, a rumor about a buyer, somebody's cousin.
Veyra tries to trace the phrase 'something interesting' backward and gets a loop of people citing each other.
Samuel recognizes the social shape immediately: expectation can aggregate without a mastermind.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Who told you something was happening here?

dialogueInline.speaker: Dylan
dialogueInline.text: Mara at South Cut.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: Mara heard it from Len.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Len told me he heard it from a caravan out of Bellweather.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: Bellweather heard about us after we left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: So there isn't one person at the beginning of this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Every piece started somewhere. That doesn't mean they all started together.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That's worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: No. It's just harder to trace.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Is there any supper left?

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: Plenty.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Then something interesting did happen.

directionInline.text: Show emergent social causality. The convergence can feel uncanny while remaining fully possible through ordinary rumor.

title: Constellations
summary: Baird warns Veyra that travelers can turn unfamiliar people into a constellation because they do not know the histories between them. Veyra accepts the criticism without abandoning the larger recurrence.

panelPlan.text: On a rooftop or high gallery, Baird points down to people Eva had marked as separate oddities and narrates the mundane ties between them.
Veyra closes one notebook but keeps another open, separating what is locally explained from what still lacks a source.
Kael joins Eva and Jessa briefly, then leaves them talking after Eva asks whether weird places make weird people or merely reveal them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: You've been here three days. I've known half those people since they were children.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: That still doesn't explain everything we've seen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Baird Rook
dialogueInline.text: Good. Throw out what I can explain and keep the rest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What if places like this collect people who would be strange anywhere?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: What if everybody is strange when you stay long enough?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Kael is strange.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Thank you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: You are not helping your case.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I didn't know I had one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: See?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Unfortunately, yes.

directionInline.text: End with a more disciplined mystery method: subtract what local knowledge explains instead of counting every unusual thing as evidence.
